title: Settings test suite is racy under Odin's parallel test runner — intermittently fails on the reviewed HEAD
evidence:
settings_test_seq: u64 // package counter — unique within the test binary

tmp_settings_path :: proc(t: ^testing.T) -> string {
	settings_test_seq += 1
	...
	path := strings.concatenate({dir, "/pp-settings-test-", fmt.tprintf("%d", settings_test_seq)}, context.temp_allocator)

Observed on this worktree (odin test app -file, runner "Starting test runner with 11 threads"):
settings: /var/folders/.../pp-settings-test-4 has a foreign format — defaults
settings: /var/folders/.../pp-settings-test-4 has a foreign format — defaults
[ERROR] --- [settings_test.odin:104:settings_mode_out_of_range_defaults()] an out-of-range palette mode must fall back to defaults
Finished 13 tests in 1.027ms. 1 test failed.
(1 failure in 6 consecutive runs; passes in isolation with -define:ODIN_TEST_NAMES=main.settings_mode_out_of_range_defaults)
detail: Odin runs @(test) procs in parallel threads; the unsynchronized package-global counter lets two tests draw the same temp path (two 'pp-settings-test-4' lines above), and interleaved fixture writes make a neighbor's file load as non-defaults. ci-local gate 2 runs 'odin test app', so the merge gate is intermittently red; the comment's 'parallel/CI runs never collide' claim is false.
recommended_fix: Drop the shared counter: give each test its own literal unique suffix (e.g. "-roundtrip", "-mode-oor"), or make the counter atomic (core:sync) and add a per-test disambiguator; re-run odin test app repeatedly to confirm.

title: Python bytecode cache committed: tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc tracked in the reviewed HEAD
evidence:
git show 70e3e91 --stat | tail:
 tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc | Bin 0 -> 13615 bytes
 tools/derive_a11y_palettes.py                          |  14 ++++++++++----

git ls-files | grep .pyc:
tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc

.gitignore contains no __pycache__/ or *.pyc entry (grep 'pycache|pyc' .gitignore → no matches).
detail: A machine-generated CPython cache artifact from running the derivation script is now version-controlled and will silently go stale against tools/derive_a11y_palettes.py on future edits; nothing in the repo ignores it.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc and add '__pycache__/' + '*.pyc' to .gitignore in the same commit.

title: SLA gauge rows scale the font but not the row pitch/rect — lines overlap each other and the tray at x1.25/x1.50, contradicting the 'every HUD surface' claim
detail: At x1.50 the gauge font is hud(16)=24px on a raw 16px pitch (DrawTextEx y is glyph top-left): rows 1-3 overlap by ~8px, the 18px focus rect is shorter than its text, and row 3 (win_h-48) lands inside the scaled tray band (win_h-54..win_h-15). x1.25 overlaps ~4px. E9.3 'chrome stays legible at each step' fails here.
recommended_fix: Route the row math through hud(): v.win_h - hud(v,80) + line*hud(v,16), scale sla_row_rect's height/width via hud_f, keeping the draw + sla_focus_click hit-test on the same rects.

title: step_of is production-dead — referenced only by its own tests despite the doc claiming panel-display/save use
detail: The helper's stated production consumers don't exist; it exists only to be tested. Misleading doc plus dead code in a new file.
recommended_fix: Either delete step_of (and its two test lines) or wire the panel's scale row save through it; fix the comment to match reality.

title: PALETTE_MODE_COUNT constant has zero references
evidence:
PALETTE_MODE_COUNT :: 4

repo-wide grep for PALETTE_MODE_COUNT: only the definition at app/render/palette.odin:22 (palcheck/parity/tests use Palette_Mode.Tritan or PALETTE_TOKEN_COUNT instead).
detail: Dead constant added with the new mode machinery; nothing reads it, so it can drift from Palette_Mode's member count unnoticed.
recommended_fix: Delete PALETTE_MODE_COUNT, or derive cycle_palette's bound from it to give it a live consumer.

title: demolish_button_rect's nil-view fallback is a second, unscaled geometry — the parity pipe-button click center uses it
detail: The project's own popover single-source rule is violated by the fallback: at ui_scale > 1 the parity click center and the app's hit rect diverge. Harmless today only because parity views run at x1.00.
recommended_fix: Pass the view at harness/parity.odin:976 (pipe_demolish_btn_center already receives one) and drop the default-nil parameter so unscaled geometry cannot be selected.
